answer: To resist Sybils, agents must maintain a unique physical beacon transmitter sealed inside a jade-hardened enclosure and mounted on a distributed trellis of peer-verified locations. The beacon broadcasts a time-locked signature that neighbors cross-check for consistent signal strength and latency. An honest agent buys one module once. An attacker seeking 200 identities must manufacture, seal, and geographically distribute 200 separate jade modules, paying both fabrication costs and ongoing logistics that scale linearly with the attack size.
